seoTitle: How to Apply for a Master's or PhD in the UK
title: How to Apply for a Master's or PhD in the UK
content:
Start with the course's own application instructions. A taught master's application and a PhD application often need different documents, and admission does not automatically include funding.

Quick overview: Find a suitable opportunity → check the university’s official requirements → prepare documents → apply through the official portal → arrange funding → meet offer conditions → apply for your visa. Use NextApply to discover opportunities, but confirm each detail with the university before applying.

1. Find the Right UK Opportunity on NextApply

Start with the UK opportunities page, then narrow your search to Master's programmes or PhD opportunities. You can also explore subjects, universities, fully funded opportunities and closing deadlines.

  • Read the listing: Note the subject, university, degree type, deadline, eligibility and funding details.
  • Check the official page: Open the university or funder link to confirm the information is current.
  • Save suitable options: Keep your shortlist on the Saved page so you can compare them.

Important: A “fully funded” label does not automatically mean all international tuition fees, living costs, travel and visa costs are covered. Check exactly what the award includes and whether international applicants are eligible.

2. Applying for a Taught Master’s (MSc, MA or Similar)

Step 1: Choose a course and check entry requirements

Open the official course page to confirm academic requirements, accepted English tests, course length, tuition fees, start date and deadline. Some courses require a UK 2:1 equivalent, while others have different entry standards. IELTS requirements vary by course; do not assume one score works everywhere.

Step 2: Prepare your application documents

  • Academic transcripts and degree certificates, with translations if required.
  • Personal statement explaining why this specific course fits your background and goals.
  • CV or résumé, where requested.
  • Academic or professional references in the number and format the university requires.
  • English-language evidence and passport details, if requested.
  • Portfolio, writing sample or professional experience evidence for courses that require them.

Step 3: Do you need to email a professor?

For most taught Master’s courses, no. Admissions teams handle applications. Contact the course admissions office if you have a question about eligibility, scholarships or documents. For an MRes or MPhil, a supervisor may be needed, so check the course instructions first.

Step 4: Apply through the official university portal

Follow the university’s application instructions, upload your documents and submit before the stated deadline. Some courses assess applications as they arrive; others have fixed rounds. Application fees and fee waivers vary, so use the amount shown in the official portal rather than relying on a general estimate.

Step 5: Understand the offer and next steps

An offer may be conditional (you must still meet requirements) or unconditional. The university may ask for a deposit, depending on the course and funding status. After the necessary conditions are met, it can issue a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) for your Student visa application.

How much does a UK Master’s cost?

International tuition fees differ substantially by university, subject and course. Laboratory-based courses and MBAs can cost more than many classroom-based programmes. Use the exact international fee shown on each official course page; also budget for accommodation, food, travel, visa charges and the immigration health surcharge.

Master’s scholarship options

  • Chevening: Competitive government-funded awards for eligible applicants; check the current country-specific criteria and application window.
  • Commonwealth Scholarships: Specific programmes for eligible Commonwealth applicants, with distinct rules and nomination processes.
  • GREAT Scholarships: Awards offered through participating universities and countries; availability changes by year.
  • University awards: Check departmental bursaries, tuition discounts and merit scholarships on the relevant university’s funding pages.

3. Applying for a PhD in the UK

Step 1: Decide between an advertised project and a proposed project

An advertised PhD usually has a defined research topic, supervisor and application procedure. A self-proposed PhD starts with your own research idea, and you may need to find an academic whose interests match it. Browse PhD opportunities and the subject directory to identify possible options.

Step 2: Check whether supervisor contact is expected

Contacting a potential supervisor is often useful, especially for self-proposed research, but it is not universally required. Some funded studentships instruct candidates to apply centrally without prior contact. Always follow the advertised project’s guidance.

When contacting a supervisor, send a concise, personalised message that explains your background, a specific connection to their research and what you would like to ask. Attach a short CV if appropriate. A positive email reply does not replace a formal university application or guarantee funding.

Step 3: Prepare a research proposal if requested

Not every advertised PhD requires a separate proposal. If it does, follow the university’s required length and structure rather than assuming a universal word count.

  • Research question and why it matters.
  • Brief context from relevant published research, with verifiable references.
  • Proposed methods, data or experiments and how you would evaluate results.
  • Feasibility, ethical considerations where relevant and a realistic timeline.
  • Why the project matches the supervisor, research group and available facilities.

Step 4: Check eligibility and submit

Review degree requirements, research experience, English-language conditions, references and any ATAS requirement. Some PhD programmes accept applicants directly after a Bachelor’s degree; others expect a Master’s. Apply via the university or studentship portal and be ready to discuss your research plans in an interview.

Step 5: Confirm the full funding package

UK PhD funding can include tuition fees, a living stipend and research or training support. However, funding at the UK Home-fee rate is not the same as funding all international fees. Check international eligibility, fee coverage, stipend duration and any additional costs before accepting an offer.

For 2026/27, the UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) minimum full-time stipend is £21,805 per year (with a higher London-weighted minimum). This is a benchmark for UKRI-funded awards, not a guarantee for every PhD scholarship. See UKRI’s official guidance.

4. Master’s vs PhD: What Is Different?

TopicTaught Master’sPhD
Main focusAdvanced coursework and sometimes a dissertationOriginal research and a thesis
Typical full-time durationOften 1 year; check the courseOften 3–4 years; check the project
Supervisor contactUsually unnecessaryOften helpful, depending on the project
Research proposalUsually not requiredSometimes required; project-dependent
How to applyUniversity course application portalUniversity / funded-project application process
FundingUniversity and external scholarships; often competitiveStudentships and scholarships; check international fee coverage
Main documentsTranscripts, statement, references and other course-specific evidenceTranscripts, references, CV and proposal if required

5. UK Student Visa: What International Applicants Need

Once you receive the required offer documentation and CAS, follow the official Student visa guidance. Your university can explain which documents apply to you. Requirements may include a valid passport, English-language evidence, financial documents, ATAS (for certain courses) and a tuberculosis test where required.

Money required for a Student visa (October 2026)

For most Student visa applicants who must demonstrate maintenance funds, the current living-cost requirement is:

Study locationPer monthMaximum for 9 months
London£1,529£13,761
Outside London£1,171£10,539

These amounts are in addition to outstanding course fees, subject to the visa rules and any permitted deductions or exemptions. Where the 28-day funds rule applies, the required money generally must be held for 28 consecutive days, with evidence dated within the prescribed period. See official financial requirements for exceptions and acceptable evidence.

The Student visa application fee is £558 as of October 2026. The immigration health surcharge is normally an additional cost. Confirm the final amount on GOV.UK when you apply.

ATAS for certain research and technical subjects

Some programmes in sensitive subject areas require an Academic Technology Approval Scheme (ATAS) certificate. The requirement depends on factors including the course and applicant’s nationality; it does not apply to every engineering or computer science student. The application is free, and official guidance says processing takes at least 30 working days, sometimes longer. Check ATAS guidance early.

Can you work in the UK after graduation?

The Graduate visa generally permits eligible Bachelor’s and Master’s graduates to stay for 2 years if they apply by 31 December 2026, or 18 months if they apply from 1 January 2027. Eligible doctoral graduates can stay for 3 years. You must meet the route’s conditions; completing a degree does not automatically grant a Graduate visa.

7. Your Application Checklist

  • Choose a suitable Master’s course or PhD project and save its official link.
  • Check eligibility, international tuition fees, funding rules and the exact deadline.
  • Prepare the documents requested for that specific application.
  • For research degrees, check whether a supervisor or proposal is required.
  • Submit using the official university or funder portal.
  • Review any offer conditions and clarify scholarship coverage before accepting.
  • Obtain your CAS and prepare Student visa evidence, including ATAS if needed.

Start Exploring UK Opportunities

Browse UK opportunities, Master's programmes, PhD opportunities or fully funded opportunities on NextApply, then follow the original institution’s instructions to apply. NextApply is a discovery platform; it is not a substitute for the university’s admission and funding decisions.

Information checked against official UK government and UKRI guidance in October 2026. Fees, rules, funding terms and deadlines can change; always verify them before applying.

Keep an application record from the start

For each course or project, save the official instructions and record the academic deadline separately from the funding deadline. Note whether a supervisor conversation is required, optional or discouraged. Track transcripts, references, language evidence and any requested proposal. When you submit, keep the confirmation and application number. If a document changes later, ask whether updates are accepted instead of submitting a second application without explanation. This small record makes it easier to respond accurately when admissions requests another document or when several funding competitions overlap.

Relevant listings and guides on NextApply

To see how these questions apply to a real listing, review AI for Biomedical Innovation CDT at University of Edinburgh 2027. Compare its stated requirements with your own preparation and check the official source before applying.

You can also browse The University of Edinburgh on NextApply and the doctoral training programmes category. Listings and recruitment windows can change.
